original_question: For the three-machine job-shop makespan problem J3||C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized jointly by p_max, the maximum processing time, and n_max, the maximum number of operations in a job?
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, Open Problem 12: "Is J3||Cmax fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the maximum processing time pmax and the maximum number nmax of operations per job?"
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the exact open problem targeted in the paper: the three-machine job shop makespan problem J3||C_max, with the joint parameterization by p_max and n_max. It also keeps the scope narrow and paper-faithful, rather than drifting to a broader shop-scheduling or variable-machine variant.
missing_details: The paper's parameters are defined on operations/jobs as p_max := max_{i,j} p_{ij}, the maximum processing time of any operation, and n_max := max_j n_j, where n_j is the number of operations in job j.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should state the job-shop model used in Section 2.1.1: each job j consists of n_j totally ordered operations o_{ij}; operation o_{ij} must be processed on a prescribed machine mu_{ij} for time p_{ij}; each job can be processed by at most one machine at a time; each machine can process at most one operation at a time.

The paper's job-shop definition allows several operations of the same job to require the same machine, and a job need not have an operation on every machine; this is implicit in the notation J3 and should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation.
The number of machines is fixed to exactly 3; it is not an additional parameter of the question.
Preemption is absent by default in the paper's notation, so the intended question concerns the standard nonpreemptive J3||C_max problem.

To make 'fixed-parameter tractable' fully explicit, the question should ask whether there is an exact algorithm for J3||C_max running in f(p_max, n_max) · poly(|I|) time (equivalently, solving the corresponding decision version in such time).
The nearby context explains why the parameterization must be joint: parameterizing J3||C_max by p_max alone is already impossible in the intended sense because even J3|p_{ij}=1|C_max is NP-hard.
refined_question: Given a nonpreemptive job-shop instance on exactly three machines, where each job j consists of n_j totally ordered operations o_{ij}, each operation o_{ij} must be processed on a prescribed machine mu_{ij} in {1,2,3} for an integer processing time p_{ij}, each job can be processed by at most one machine at a time, and each machine can process at most one operation at a time, let p_max := max_{i,j} p_{ij} and n_max := max_j n_j. Is the makespan minimization problem J3||C_max fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the joint parameter (p_max, n_max)?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it matches Open Problem 12 in Section 5.1 almost verbatim. Section 5.1 first explains that p_max and n_max are the natural parameters for fixed-machine shop scheduling after earlier hardness results rely on an unbounded number of machines, and then it notes that p_max alone cannot work for J3 because J3|p_{ij}=1|C_max is NP-hard, which leads directly to Open Problem 12. Section 2.1.1 supplies the hidden notation needed to make the question fully stand-alone, especially the meanings of J3, n_j, p_{ij}, and the job-shop constraints.
